git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): the trailing element took three shapes, and two readings each had half of it

A second differential sweep — 26 fresh programs over the streams surface — found
five disagreements. Four are fixed here.

THE TRAILING ELEMENT. A file whose last byte is a newline yields one more element
than it has lines, and WHAT that element is depends on two flags at once. MEASURED
over the whole 6 file shapes × 8 flags matrix on `php -n` 8.5.6:

    no SKIP_EMPTY               it is ""
    SKIP_EMPTY, no READ_AHEAD   it is false
    SKIP_EMPTY and READ_AHEAD   there is none

Two earlier readings of this each had one row and neither varied `READ_AHEAD`: one
shipped "SKIP_EMPTY removes it", the other "SKIP_EMPTY leaves it as an empty
string". Both were half right, and the corpus caught the swap — three programs went
red on the first attempt here, which is what said the missing variable was the
read-ahead.

SKIP_EMPTY WITH DROP_NEW_LINE also skips blank lines, and the keys of what follows
are CONSECUTIVE. Under `READ_CSV` the opposite holds — php steps over the blank
RECORD and leaves the keys unchanged, `0, 2, 3` — so the line filter yields to it.

`seek()` was unbounded in both directions. A negative line is a `ValueError` in php,
not a silent rewind to `key() === -1`. Past the end php clamps the key to the last
element and leaves the object INVALID, because it walked the stream to get there and
the walk consumed it — and seeking exactly TO the last element differs from seeking
past it, which is what a single clamp would have got wrong.

A STAT-BACKED `SplFileInfo` GETTER THROWS for a path it cannot stat: all nine of
them, `RuntimeException: SplFileInfo::getSize(): stat failed for nope.txt`, with
`getType()` saying `Lstat` instead. elephc answered `0` or `false` in silence, so a
program that trusted `getSize()` got a size of zero for a file that was not there.

`file_put_contents($p, $handle)` DRAINS the stream. elephc converted the handle to a
string and wrote the fourteen bytes of `Resource id #5` where php wrote the eleven
of the content.

Verified: the sweep is 74/78 identical with 0 refusals, the 183-program round-8
corpus is unchanged at 180, and 275 `spl::`, 1097 `io::` and 1535 unit tests pass.

The four sweep programs still differing are each recorded: `feof()` on a `php://temp`
stream after the last byte, the location and frame an SPL-raised exception reports,
and `echo` on an `iterable`-typed parameter raising no `Array to string conversion`.

Two more found and left open, both outside the streams surface:
`$e` cannot be reassigned from a caught `Throwable` to another class (php allows it),
and `$obj->$name()` resolves only the first call in a loop before failing with
`callable array did not resolve to an invokable target`.
